newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela's Provincial denies Banco Bilbao buyout.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela's Provincial denies Banco Bilbao buyout.

text.p: The president of leading Venezuelan bank Banco Provincial has denied in a newspaper interview that Spanish bank Banco Bilbao Vizcaya has bought a controlling stake in the bank.
Provincial President Jose Maria Nogueroles flatly denied a report in evening paper El Mundo on Tuesday that Banco Bilbao had bought a 51 percent stake in Venezuela's largest bank.
"At the moment I don't have any information that any sale of. shares has taken place," Nogueroles told El Universal in a story published Wednesday.

A report in daily El Nacional on Wednesday said Banco Bilbao Vizcaya was seeking to buy about 30 percent of Provincial, currently owned between French bank Credit Lyonnais and U.S.- based financier guru George Soros.
Over the past two year Credit Lyonnais has continued to divest itself of financial investments made around the world, reducing its international presence by between 25 and 30 percent.

Credit Lyonnais holds about 18 percent of Provincial. George Soros bought over nine percent of the bank in February 1996. Local brewing group Polar, which recently signed to bottle Pepsi in Venezuela, owns another 40 percent of the bank.
El Nacional said a 30 percent stake in Provincial would cost around $60 million.
Banco Provincial held one trillion bolivars in deposits at the end of October, according to Softline financial consultants, nearly a quarter of Venezuela's total deposits.
